candidates.title: Pulmonary edema during cesarean delivery secondary to Takotsubo syndrome revealing pheochromocytoma: a case report.
candidates.abstract: Acute pulmonary edema during delivery is a serious condition with a wide range of etiologies, including Takotsubo syndrome (TTS), a form of transient left ventricular dysfunction most often presenting as apical ballooning. We report the case of a 35-year-old woman who developed severe hypertension (205/130 mmHg), polypnea, and a drop in oxygen saturation to 80% during cesarean delivery under spinal anesthesia. She received noninvasive ventilation while the cesarean section continued and was transferred to the intensive care unit. Point-of-care ultrasound showed a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 35% with apical ballooning and diffuse B-lines on lung ultrasound. Computed tomography identified a right adrenal mass. A diagnosis of pulmonary edema complicating TTS was made, and the patient received furosemide and oxygen therapy. Further investigations, including urinary catecholamine metabolites, confirmed the diagnosis of pheochromocytoma. One week later, LVEF had recovered to 57% with mild residual apical hypokinesia and complete clinical recovery. The patient was then transferred to the surgical unit for management of the pheochromocytoma. This case demonstrates that TTS can cause pulmonary edema in the peripartum period, and that timely diagnosis is essential for a favorable outcome. Point-of-care ultrasound can be instrumental in guiding the assessment of such critical situations, and noninvasive ventilation may be of particular value in selected pregnant patients. This case also underscores the importance of an etiological workup and prompt treatment of hypertensive disorders in pregnancy, especially when pheochromocytoma is suspected, since anesthesia and surgery can precipitate decompensation.

candidates.title: Diagnostic delay length and disease severity are the main predictors of sleep apnea in acromegaly patients.
candidates.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) affects up to 80% of patients at diagnosis of acromegaly and often persists despite treatment. Currently, patients at risk for OSA are recommended to be identified to offer polygraphy evaluation. To study the prevalence and risk factors for OSA in patients with acromegaly. Prospective, single-center study; polygraphy was performed on 36 patients with acromegaly (age 54.1 ± 12.9 years). OSA was found in 17 patients (47.2%), mostly mild (64.7%). Patients with OSA were older both at diagnosis (p = 0.02) and at polygraphy (p = 0.008), had a longer diagnostic delay (p = 0.003) and higher BMI (p = 0.03). Patients with uncontrolled acromegaly exhibited a significantly higher number of apneas (p=0.02) and obstructive apneas (p=0.04) and had significantly lower minimum oxygen saturations (p=0.02) and a higher percentage of time spent with oxygen saturation <90% (p=0.03) as compared to those with full disease control. Diagnostic delay was the best predictor of apnea-ipopnea index (AHI, p=0.04) and oxygen desaturation index (ODI, p=0.04) scores, independently on BMI. Insulin resistance (p = 0.05), glucose profile impairment (p = 0.05) and STOP-Bang score (p=0.001), but not Epworth Sleepiness Scale score (p = 0.96), were significantly higher in patients with OSA as compared to those without. Diagnostic delay and patients' age, rather than disease status, appear to predict the development of OSA and influence its severity. These findings reinforce the importance of early identification of patients at higher risk for OSA.

candidates.title: Newborn Screening for X-Linked Adrenoleukodystrophy: A Systematic Literature Review.
candidates.abstract: X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy (X-ALD) is the most common leukodystrophy and peroxisomal disorder. It was added to newborn screening (NBS) programs following its first implementation in New York in 2013. Since then, X-ALD screening has expanded rapidly, although important differences exist among programs. This systematic review aimed to evaluate the global implementation of NBS for X-ALD, including screening methodologies, screening performance, prevalence estimates, genetic findings, and clinical follow-up outcomes. A systematic search of PubMed and EMBASE identified 13 publications describing NBS programs conducted between 2013 and June 2026. All programs used C26:0-lysophosphatidylcholine (C26:0-LPC) as the primary biomarker, although substantial heterogeneity was observed in analytical methodologies, cut-off values, screening algorithms, and follow-up strategies. Positive predictive values ranged from 9.1% to 100%, while screening detection rates varied from 1:3118 to 1:51,081, reflecting differences in study design, screening population, sample size, and screening approaches. Variants of uncertain significance (VUS) accounted for 52.6% of individuals detected with classified ABCD1 variant findings, representing a major challenge for genetic counseling and clinical management. Most identified newborns were asymptomatic at diagnosis, supporting the role of NBS in enabling early surveillance for adrenal insufficiency and cerebral disease before irreversible manifestations occur. In addition, differences between universal and sex-specific screening strategies highlight ongoing clinical and ethical debates regarding the scope of X-ALD NBS. Overall, current evidence supports the feasibility of NBS for X-ALD and its ability to enable presymptomatic ascertainment and early clinical surveillance; however, greater harmonization of screening protocols, improved variant interpretation, and long-term outcome studies are needed to optimize program performance and clinical benefit.

candidates.title: An Overview of Cushing's Syndrome Caused by Ectopic Adrenocorticotropin Secretion.
candidates.abstract: Ectopic Cushing's syndrome (ECS) causes 10% to 20% of all cases of endogenous hypercortisolism. It is caused by the aberrant secretion of adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) or corticotropin-releasing hormone (CRH) due to the presence of an ectopic tumor. The latter is usually a neuroendocrine (NEN) tumor (mostly thoracic NENs such as bronchial NEN neoplasms, thymic NEN neoplasms, small cell lung carcinoma (SCLC), or pancreatic NEN neoplasms). Clinical presentation is heterogeneous: an aggressive phenotype, typically driven by rapidly growing, poorly differentiated tumors such as small-cell lung carcinoma, manifests with severe symptoms of acute onset, predominant myopathy, resistant arterial hypertension, hypokalemia, and severe hyperpigmentation, usually without the centripetal obesity typical of Cushing's syndrome; conversely, an indolent phenotype, more often related to well-differentiated neuroendocrine neoplasms such as bronchial carcinoids, may present with the classic centripetal fat distribution, facial plethora, and purple striae also seen in Cushing's disease, making clinical distinction between the two difficult. The diagnosis of ECS can be cumbersome and time-consuming. Once hypercortisolism is confirmed, the most critical step is to distinguish patients with an ectopic source of ACTH from those with pituitary adenoma. Dynamic endocrine tests such as the high-dose dexamethasone suppression test, CRH stimulation tests, desmopressin tests, and bilateral inferior petrosal sinus sampling (BIPSS) can be helpful in the differential diagnosis. BIPSS is considered the gold standard for distinguishing a pituitary from a non-pituitary source of ACTH: the absence of a central-to-peripheral ACTH gradient supports, but does not by itself localize or confirm, an ectopic source. Tumor localization is achieved by a multimodality imaging protocol, including initial high-resolution computed tomography (CT) scans, followed by functional imaging, mainly Gallium-68-labeled somatostatin receptor positron emission tomography (PET)/CT scans. However, in 10-20% of these patients, the tumors cannot be localized. The treatment of ACTH-dependent hypercortisolism is two-fold: one is to immediately control hypercortisolism to prevent life-threatening complications (opportunistic infections and thromboembolism), and the second is to definitively treat the tumor. Medical treatment with steroidogenesis inhibitors, including metyrapone, ketoconazole, and osilodrostat, or surgical management (bilateral adrenalectomy) can be effective in immediately controlling hypercortisolism. Definitive surgical resection of the tumor is the hoped-for final treatment. The prognosis is variable, depending on the nature of the underlying neoplasm, ranging from excellent in patients with resected bronchial carcinoids to dismal in those with SCLC.

candidates.title: Acinetobacter baumannii Nosocomial Meningitis Secondary to Neurosurgical Intervention: A Case Report.
candidates.abstract: Nosocomial meningitis is a serious complication of neurosurgical procedures, associated with high morbidity and mortality, as well as significant diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. Among the causative pathogens, Acinetobacter baumannii (A. baumannii) is particularly concerning due to its ability to survive for prolonged periods in the hospital environment, its opportunistic virulence, and, especially, its tendency to develop multidrug resistance to antimicrobial agents. Diagnosis is often difficult in the postoperative setting, particularly when the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) is altered as a result of the surgical procedure. Rapid identification of the causative agent and early initiation of appropriate antibiotic therapy are essential to limit complications and improve patient prognosis. We report the case of a 27-year-old patient with a history of surgically treated craniopharyngioma complicated by anterior hypopituitarism. Three weeks after surgery, he was admitted to the ICU with suspected postoperative meningitis due to the onset of behavioral disturbances associated with nasal discharge, without a fever. Brain CT was normal. CSF analysis, obtained by lumbar puncture under strict aseptic conditions, revealed a turbid fluid with leukocytosis of 5,760 cells/mm³, predominantly composed of neutrophils, along with elevated protein levels (5.7 g/L) and low glucose levels (0.05 g/L). Direct examination after Gram staining showed Gram-negative coccobacilli with a marked inflammatory reaction. CSF culture grew a multidrug-resistant (MDR) strain of A. baumannii, which was sensitive only to colistin. The patient received antibiotic therapy with colistin, administered intravenously and intrathecally for 18 days, with initial neurological improvement and sterilization of the CSF by the 15th day of treatment. The subsequent course was unfavorable, marked by the development of acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) secondary to ventilator-associated pneumonia caused by methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), complicated by refractory septic shock, which ultimately led to his death after one month of hospitalization in the ICU. This report highlights the severity of nosocomial meningitis caused by MDR A. baumannii and underscores the importance of implementing infection prevention measures in healthcare settings.

candidates.title: Pegvisomant in severe, treatment-resistant thyroid eye disease: a case report.
candidates.abstract: Teprotumumab, a monoclonal antibody against the IGF1 receptor, has proven effective in the treatment of thyroid eye disease (TED). Pegvisomant reduces IGF1 levels through selective inhibition of growth hormone receptors. Here, we present a hypothesis-generating case of a 69-year-old patient with progressive TED. Pegvisomant 20 mg was administered daily for 90 days. IGF1 levels declined and remained low-normal during treatment. Clinical activity scores and VISA (vision, inflammation, strabismus and appearance) scores improved rapidly. MRI assessment showed that water content of both extraocular muscles and orbital connective tissue decreased after treatment. 99mTc-DTPA SPECT confirmed the decrease in disease activity. Further studies may confirm the efficacy of pegvisomant in TED. A 69-year-old female patient with severe, active thyroid eye disease (TED) – a condition linked to Graves’ disease where the body’s immune system attacks tissues around the eyes – presented with bulging eyes (proptosis), double vision, eye redness, swelling and reduced visual sharpness.Prior treatments with standard therapies for TED, including intravenous steroid courses, radiation therapy targeting the orbit (eye socket) and the biological drug rituximab, failed to achieve improvement. TED progresses in part because proteins called IGF1 receptors on the surface of eye-socket tissues are overactivated. The researchers hypothesized that using pegvisomant, which is a medication typically used for acromegaly (hormone imbalance) that lowers insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF1) levels in the blood, would reduce activation of these receptors and ease eye inflammation.The patient received a daily 20 mg injection of pegvisomant for 90 days. Symptom improvement The patient experienced a rapid reduction in eye pain, redness and swelling, alongside marked improvement in visual sharpness and colour vision within 8 weeks.MRI and imaging results Orbital MRI and nuclear imaging showed a distinct drop in tissue inflammation and fluid accumulation (oedema) in the muscles around the eye.Proptosis and double vision Eye bulging and double vision did not significantly change during the trial.Safety Pegvisomant was well tolerated with no reported side effects, and her blood sugar and liver function remained stable. Blood IGF1 levels dropped as expected and returned to normal after treatment ended. Pegvisomant rapidly reduced eye inflammation and improved vision in a patient whose TED had resisted standard therapies. However, because this was a single case study, the delayed effects from previous treatments cannot be entirely ruled out. Further clinical trials are needed to determine if pegvisomant is effective at higher doses or when given earlier in the disease course.

candidates.title: Long-term post-trial extension of osilodrostat therapy in selected Canadian patients with Cushing disease from the LINC 3 and LINC 4 programs.
candidates.abstract: Long-term outcomes of selected patients who continue osilodrostat for Cushing disease after clinical-trial participation remain incompletely described. We retrospectively analyzed a selected multicenter post-trial cohort of Canadian patients with Cushing disease previously enrolled in LINC 3 (NCT02180217) or LINC 4 (NCT02697734) who continued osilodrostat in the global roll-over study and, when applicable, in a Canadian investigator-initiated extension phase (ISS-CA-2023; NCT06131580). The dataset included 11 Canadian osilodrostat-exposed LINC participants who entered post-trial roll-over follow-up; 7 subsequently entered the Canadian investigator-initiated extension, whereas 4 discontinued during earlier follow-up for defined reasons. For longitudinal efficacy analyses, baseline and time zero were defined as first osilodrostat exposure in the parent LINC study; week 14 refers to week 14 after osilodrostat initiation. The main outcomes were time to first mean urinary free cortisol (mUFC) control, durability of control, long-term dose evolution, pituitary tumor surveillance, and safety. Eleven selected Canadian patients received continued osilodrostat, and all achieved first biochemical control after a median of 5 weeks (range: 2-12). Median mUFC decreased from 2.65 × ULN at parent-study baseline to 0.56 × ULN at week 14; these descriptive values were not used for inferential testing. Seven patients remained on therapy long term; at the last follow-up, six of seven had controlled mUFC after a median exposure of 98 months (range: 83 to 121). Maintenance doses varied widely, with a median last-visit dose of 6 mg/day (range: 0.125 to 40), and several patients required progressive down-titration over time. Hypocortisolism/adrenal-insufficiency events were common and generally managed with dose interruption or reduction and temporary glucocorticoid replacement. Clinically significant pituitary tumor enlargement leading to discontinuation and surgery occurred in two patients. In this selected Canadian post-trial continuation cohort, osilodrostat was associated with rapid initial biochemical control and durable long-term control in many patients for up to 10 years. The findings support the feasibility of long-term individualized osilodrostat management in selected patients continuing therapy after LINC 3/LINC 4 participation, with ongoing need for dose adaptation and surveillance for adrenal insufficiency and pituitary tumor behavior.

candidates.title: A Case of MEN 2A Syndrome With Bilateral Recurrent Pheochromocytoma: A Case Report and Literature Review.
candidates.abstract: Pheochromocytoma is a neuroendocrine tumor arising from chromaffin cells and producing catecholamines. Due to the excessive release of catecholamines, these tumors can present with paroxysmal episodes of high blood pressure, headache, diaphoresis, and palpitations. We present the case of a 23-year-old female patient who presented to the clinic with a history of headache, palpitations, and vomiting for two months. She was admitted for further investigations and management. Laboratory studies revealed elevated urinary and plasma catecholamine levels. Further work-up revealed bilateral adrenal masses diagnosed as pheochromocytoma and medullary thyroid cancer. The patient was diagnosed with multiple endocrine neoplasia (MEN) type 2 and underwent bilateral laparoscopic adrenalectomy and total thyroidectomy with central and lateral neck dissection, and during surveillance, she was found to have recurrent pheochromocytoma. We also discuss the diagnosis and management of recurrent pheochromocytoma in MEN syndrome.

candidates.title: Production of in vitro bovine embryos supplemented with l-carnitine in different oxygen tensions and the relation to nitric oxide.
candidates.abstract: The aim of this study was to evaluate the production of bovine embryos in vitro when supplemented with l-carnitine for 24 h beginning on day 5 (d 5) under two different oxygen tensions (20% or 5%) and the relationship of nitric oxide (NO) in in vitro culture (IVC) medium to embryo development. Cumulus-oocyte complexes (COC; n = 837) were matured in vitro for 24 h and fertilization was performed for 18 h. Zygotes were cultured in vitro for 9 days after in vitro fertilization in synthetic oviductal fluid (SOF) medium with 5% fetal calf serum. At d 5 the plates were assigned to one of four treatment groups: high (20%) or low (5%) O2 tension either with or without the addition of 3.03 mM l-carnitine (High-Cont, High-Lcar, Low-Cont, Low-Lcar). The concentration of NO in the culture medium was evaluated on d 5, d 6 and d 9. On d 7, parts of the embryos were submitted for evaluation of intracellular lipid droplets. The cleavage rate was similar (P > 0.05) between high and low O2 tension and the blastocyst rate was similar in all conditions evaluated. The hatching rate was higher (P < 0.05) for Low-Cont. The NO concentration was higher at d 9 under low O2 tension (P < 0.1). The addition of 3.03 mM l-carnitine between d 5 and d 6 of IVC was not efficient in reducing cytoplasmic lipid content of bovine embryos. Additionally, IVC at a low oxygen tension without l-carnitine promoted better conditions for embryo development. A higher concentration of NO in medium was observed under low O2 tension.

candidates.title: Retrospective Evaluation of a New Danish National Guideline: Impact on Neonatal Hypoglycemia and Breastfeeding.
candidates.abstract: This study evaluates the impact of the most recent Danish national guideline for the management of neonatal hypoglycemia on neonate nutrition at discharge and the incidence of neonatal hypoglycaemia within the first 24 h postpartum. The updated guideline introduced a 50% reduction in early feeding volume to support exclusive breastfeeding and implemented Dextrogel as first-line treatment for neonatal hypoglycaemia. This retrospective cohort study compared two groups of neonates with increased risk of hypoglycemia: Group 2020 (n = 254), managed according to the 2019 guideline, and Group 2024 (n = 217), managed under the 2023 guideline. The primary outcome was nutrition at discharge; the secondary outcome was the incidence of neonatal hypoglycaemia within 24 h postpartum. A significant difference was observed in nutrition at discharge, with 59% (151/254) of neonates in 2020 being breastfed compared to 68% (148/217) in 2024 (p = 0.05). The overall incidence of neonatal hypoglycaemia was also significantly different: 23% (58/254) in 2020 versus 31% (67/217) in 2024 (p = 0.05). Significant differences were similarly observed at 1, 2 and 12 h postpartum. The revised guideline appears to support breastfeeding, with a higher proportion of neonates breastfed at discharge. Despite an increased incidence of neonatal hypoglycaemia, cases were transient and effectively managed with Dextrogel.

candidates.title: Evaluation of Diastolic Dysfunction in Pituitary Adenomas: A Comparative Single-Center Study Among Acromegaly, Prolactinoma, and Nonfunctioning Pituitary Adenomas.
candidates.abstract: Background and Objectives: Pituitary adenomas may be associated with metabolic and cardiovascular abnormalities, but comparative evidence across subtypes is limited. We compared cardiometabolic and echocardiographic profiles, left ventricular diastolic dysfunction (LVDD), and carotid intima-media thickness (CIMT) among patients with prolactinoma, acromegaly, or nonfunctioning pituitary adenoma (NFPA) and healthy controls and investigated factors associated with LVDD. Materials and Methods: This cross-sectional comparative study included 214 participants evaluated between 2016 and 2018: 91 with prolactinoma, 26 with acromegaly, 45 with NFPA, and 52 healthy controls. Participants underwent clinical, biochemical, echocardiographic, and CIMT assessment. LVDD was diagnosed and graded according to the 2016 American Society of Echocardiography (ASE) and European Association of Cardiovascular Imaging (EACVI) recommendations. Factors associated with LVDD were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression. Results: The mean age was 41.3 ± 12.4 years, and 64.5% of participants were women. Acromegaly was associated with the highest fasting glucose, HbA1c, insulin, and homeostasis model assessment of insulin resistance (HOMA-IR) values (all p < 0.001) and, compared with controls, a higher left atrial volume index (LAVI) and average E/e' ratio and lower left ventricular ejection fraction (despite preserved ejection fraction), E/A ratio, and lateral e' velocity. CIMT was higher in NFPA than in prolactinoma. LVDD was present in 21.5% of the cohort and in 5.8%, 19.8%, 46.2%, and 28.9% of the control, prolactinoma, acromegaly, and NFPA groups, respectively (p < 0.001); 84.8% of cases were grade I. Increasing age was independently associated with LVDD (OR 1.265 per year, 95% CI 1.155-1.385; p < 0.001), and diagnostic group was independently associated with LVDD overall (p = 0.004). Compared with controls, adjusted LVDD odds were higher in prolactinoma (OR 10.9, 95% CI 1.34-89.68), acromegaly (OR 167.5, 95% CI 10.3-2721.4), and NFPA (OR 12.0, 95% CI 1.4-104.8). Conclusions: Pituitary adenoma subtypes were associated with distinct cardiometabolic and echocardiographic profiles and a higher prevalence of LVDD than in healthy controls, particularly in acromegaly. Most LVDD cases were grade I, indicating predominantly impaired relaxation. Although age and diagnostic group were associated with LVDD in the adjusted analysis, the wide confidence intervals warrant cautious interpretation and validation in larger cohorts.

candidates.title: Mild Autonomous Cortisol Secretion Is Associated with Computed Tomography-Derived Hepatic Steatosis in Patients with Adrenal Incidentaloma.
candidates.abstract: Background and Objectives: Mild autonomous cortisol secretion (MACS) has been associated with adverse metabolic outcomes, but its relationship with hepatic steatosis remains incompletely understood. This study aimed to compare computed tomography (CT)-derived hepatic steatosis parameters between patients with MACS and non-functioning adrenal incidentaloma (NFAI) and to evaluate the associations between biochemical markers of cortisol secretion and hepatic attenuation measures. Materials and Methods: This retrospective study comprised 123 patients with adrenal incidentaloma (39 MACS and 84 NFAI) who underwent unenhanced abdominal CT between January 2020 and November 2024. Hepatic steatosis was assessed using mean liver attenuation, liver-spleen attenuation difference, liver-to-spleen attenuation ratio, and conventional CT-defined steatosis thresholds. Non-invasive metabolic indices were also computed. Associations between cortisol secretion parameters and CT-derived hepatic attenuation measures were examined using correlation analysis and multivariable regression. Results: The liver-to-spleen attenuation ratio was lower in the MACS group, although this difference did not reach statistical significance (p = 0.050), and a significantly lower liver-spleen attenuation difference (p = 0.048) was observed compared with the NFAI group, whereas mean liver attenuation (p = 0.167), conventional CT-defined hepatic steatosis, and non-invasive metabolic indices did not differ significantly between groups. Among biochemical markers of cortisol secretion, only 24-h urinary free cortisol showed significant correlations with all CT-derived hepatic attenuation parameters. After adjustment for age, sex, and BMI, urinary free cortisol remained significantly associated with liver-spleen attenuation difference (p = 0.047), whereas its associations with liver attenuation (p = 0.056) and liver-to-spleen attenuation ratio (p = 0.051) did not reach statistical significance. Conclusions: Patients with MACS exhibit subtle CT-derived hepatic fat accumulation despite similar conventional CT-defined steatosis and non-invasive metabolic indices compared with patients with NFAI. Continuous CT-derived attenuation parameters may be more sensitive than conventional CT-defined steatosis thresholds for detecting subtle hepatic fat accumulation associated with mild cortisol excess. The consistent associations observed between 24-h urinary free cortisol and CT-derived hepatic attenuation parameters, including the significant association with liver-spleen attenuation difference after adjustment for age, sex, and BMI, warrant confirmation in larger prospective studies.

candidates.title: Beyond the Operating Room: A Health-System Framework for Sustainable Kidney Transplant Care across Pakistan and Comparable Low- and Middle-Income Countries.
candidates.abstract: Kidney transplant care in low- and middle-income countries still prioritises getting patients to transplant over the systems needed to sustain long-term graft survival. This narrative review argues that graft survival is best understood as a health-system outcome rather than a purely surgical one, drawing on evidence from Pakistan, India, Iran, Brazil, and Türkiye. We searched major databases through July 2026 and grey literature through September 2026 for evidence on post-transplant maintenance care, funding, surveillance, and outcomes across these countries. We organised what we found around the World Health Organization's health-system building blocks. On the basis of our results, we propose the Graft Survivorship Framework: five interdependent domains covering lifelong access to immunosuppression and medication continuity, follow-up and surveillance infrastructure, service delivery and continuity of care, governance and funding, and equity-focused outcome tracking. The framework most directly applies to middle-income systems with established transplant programmes, and may serve as a guide for low-income countries as their programmes expand. In the published evidence we reviewed, no single country's system addressed all five domains, but each illustrates a distinct policy approach, whether centralised funding, institution-driven care, or national outcome registries. Because these domains depend on one another, weakness in any one may undermine the rest, even when the others are strong. Translating this framework into context-specific policy, and testing it prospectively, may offer a practical way toward more durable and equitable transplant outcomes in comparable settings.

candidates.title: Newly Diagnosed Graves' Disease Followed by the Discovery of a Cavernous Internal Carotid Artery Aneurysm Causing Panhypopituitarism: A Case Report.
candidates.abstract: Sellar and parasellar vascular lesions are rare causes of pituitary dysfunction and may mimic pituitary adenomas or other sellar masses. Cavernous internal carotid artery (ICA) aneurysms can cause hypopituitarism through compression of the pituitary gland or stalk, but diagnosis may be delayed when symptoms are initially attributed to a more common endocrine disorder. We report a 37-year-old man who presented with six weeks of unintentional weight loss, fatigue, heat intolerance, excessive sweating, anxiety, tremor, and tachycardia. Initial evaluation showed suppressed thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH), elevated total triiodothyronine (T3), positive thyrotropin receptor antibody, positive thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulin, and a hypervascular thyroid gland on ultrasound, consistent with Graves' disease. He was started on methimazole and atenolol. Although thyroid function tests improved, he developed persistent neck discomfort, prompting contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT), which revealed an enhancing sellar mass. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) showed a T2-hypointense sellar lesion with internal flow artifact, and CT angiography confirmed a saccular aneurysm of the cavernous segment of the right ICA. Pituitary hormone evaluation demonstrated secondary adrenal insufficiency, central hypothyroidism, hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, growth hormone (GH) deficiency, and mild hyperprolactinemia, consistent with panhypopituitarism from pituitary compression. The patient was started on prednisone and levothyroxine, and atenolol and prednisone were subsequently discontinued before endovascular embolization was performed. At follow-up, symptoms improved, but panhypopituitarism persisted. This case highlights the importance of reassessing patients when endocrine symptoms evolve despite an initially appropriate diagnosis.

candidates.title: Proteomic profiling of somatotropinoma subtypes reveals TNIP1 overexpression in sparsely granulated tumors in a small discovery cohort.
candidates.abstract: The molecular mechanisms underlying the clinical differences between densely granulated (DG) and sparsely granulated (SG) somatotroph tumors remain poorly understood. To identify significant molecular differences between these subtypes, we performed quantitative mass spectrometry-based proteomic profiling followed by validation of the differentially-identified proteins. Label-free quantitative proteomic analysis was performed on SG somatotroph adenomas (SGSAs, n = 3) and DG somatotroph adenomas (DGSAs, n = 3), with each sample analyzed in technical triplicate. Key findings were subsequently validated using immunohistochemistry (IHC, n = 64), immunofluorescence (IF, n = 24), and Western blotting (WB, n = 18). Proteomic profiling identified TNFAIP3-interacting protein 1 (TNIP1) as the most significantly over-expressed protein, and coenzyme Q6 monooxygenase (COQ6) as the most significantly under-expressed protein, in SGSAs compared with DGSAs. Higher TNIP1 expression in SGSAs was significantly associated with IGF-1 [%ULN], larger tumor diameter, greater tumor volume, higher Knosp grade and SSTR5 expression. In contrast, COQ6 expression showed significant negative correlations with tumor diameter, tumor volume, Knosp grade, and SSTR5 expression. These findings indicate strong associations between TNIP1 and COQ6 expression and tumor characteristics, along with differences in cell adhesion and signaling pathways. SGSAs and DGSAs exhibit distinct proteomic profiles. Increased TNIP1 and reduced COQ6 expression, together with alterations in cell adhesion and signaling pathways in SGSA, may contribute to the molecular and phenotypic differences underlying these somatotroph tumor subtypes.

candidates.title: Retinal Microvascular and Peripapillary Profiles in Mild Autonomous Cortisol Secretion Versus Nonfunctioning Adrenal Adenomas.
candidates.abstract: Background/Objectives: Mild autonomous cortisol secretion (MACS) is associated with increased cardiometabolic morbidity, but its relationship with the retinal microcirculation is unknown. We compared retinal and peripapillary microvascular parameters between MACS and nonfunctioning adrenal adenoma (NFA) and, secondarily, examined their associations with continuously modeled post-dexamethasone cortisol. Methods: In this single-center, retrospective, cross-sectional study, 98 patients (45 NFA, 53 MACS) were included, and optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) and structural OCT data from one eye per patient were analyzed. The primary outcome was whole-image deep capillary plexus (DCP) vessel density. Multivariable models were adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, and cardiometabolic comorbidities; secondary analyses were corrected using the Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (q values). Results: OCTA was evaluable in 89 patients. The primary outcome did not differ significantly between groups in the main analysis (NFA vs. MACS, 48.64 ± 5.71% vs. 47.31 ± 5.77%; adjusted difference -1.29 percentage points, 95% CI -3.97 to 1.38; p = 0.339) or in any sensitivity analysis. In secondary analyses, superior retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL) thickness was greater in MACS (β = 17.38 µm; q < 0.001) and increased with ln(post-dexamethasone cortisol) (β = 13.74 µm; q = 0.010). Higher ln(post-dexamethasone cortisol) was also associated with lower parafoveal DCP (β = -2.72 percentage points; p = 0.013) and inside-disc radial peripapillary capillary vessel density (β = -3.13 percentage points; p = 0.026), which did not survive multiplicity correction; no superficial capillary plexus sector was associated with either exposure (all p ≥ 0.37). Conclusions: MACS was not significantly associated with whole-image DCP vessel density. The secondary associations with continuous cortisol are cross-sectional and hypothesis-generating and require prospective confirmation.

candidates.title: "Paraneoplastic syndromes secondary to Νeuroendocrine Νeoplasms".
candidates.abstract: Paraneoplastic syndromes (PNS) represent uncommon but clinically significant manifestations of neuroendocrine neoplasms (NENs) arising from ectopic hormone secretion, aberrant peptide processing, cytokine-mediated effects, or immune-mediated mechanisms. Although NENs are intrinsically capable of producing bioactive substances leading to PNS, the true prevalence of PNS in NENs remains uncertain and is likely underestimated. Paraneoplastic manifestations may precede tumor diagnosis, represent the first indication of an otherwise occult neoplasm, or emerge during disease progression, thereby providing valuable diagnostic, prognostic, and therapeutic information. Endocrine PNS, including ectopic adrenocorticotrophic hormone secretion, carcinoid syndrome, paraneoplastic hypercalcemia, syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone secretion, hypoglycemia and ectopic acromegaly, account for the majority of cases, whereas neurological PNS are rarer and predominantly associated with high-grade neuroendocrine carcinomas (NECs). Recent advances in molecular biology have revealed the importance of neuroendocrine lineage plasticity, transcriptional dysregulation, epigenetic reprogramming, and abnormal prohormone processing in the pathogenesis of these syndromes. Concurrently, improvements in biochemical testing, functional imaging, liquid biopsy technologies, and molecular profiling have enhanced diagnostic accuracy and disease monitoring. Management requires a multidisciplinary approach combining syndrome-directed therapies with tumor-targeted interventions, including surgery, somatostatin analogs, peptide receptor radionuclide therapy, targeted agents, specific chemotherapy regimens and emerging immunotherapeutic strategies. Despite substantial progress, significant gaps remain regarding epidemiology, accurate biomarkers, prognostic significance, and optimal management. This review summarizes current knowledge on pathophysiology, clinical spectrum, diagnosis, prognostic implications, and treatment of PNS associated with gastroenteropancreatic and lung NENs, while highlighting future research priorities and unmet clinical needs.

candidates.title: Disease-associated respiratory microbiota and metabolome changes in children with mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia.
candidates.abstract: BackgroundMycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia (MPP) is the most common community-acquired pneumonia in children. It is clinically characterized by insidious symptoms and common extrapulmonary complications. Severe patients are susceptible to pulmonary necrosis, pulmonary embolism, and bronchiolitis obliterans leading to permanent lung impairment.ObjectivesExploring changes in the airway microenvironment of children with MPP.DesignA prospective observational study was conducted to explore changes in the airway microenvironment of children with MPP.MethodsIn this study, 16S ribosomal RNA (rRNA) analysis and Metabolomics were used to analyze patient-derived bronchoalveolar lavage fluid to investigate changes in the airway microenvironment of patients with MPP.ResultsMicrobiomics indicates characteristics such as reduced microbial diversity and altered abundance of specific genera against the background of Mycoplasma pneumoniae infection. The metabolomics analysis can identify changes in the host metabolite profile, including abnormal levels of glycerophospholipids and sphingolipids.ConclusionIntegrating multi-omics data to elucidate the microbiota-metabolite-host interaction network may provide new strategies for precise classification, severe warning, and targeted therapy for MPP. We performed a clinical cohort study utilizing bronchoalveolar lavage fluid samples to examine changes in airway microbiota and host-Mycoplasma interactions in pediatric patients with mycoplasma pneumonia, with the objective of facilitating early identification and intervention for severe cases of mycoplasma pneumonia.

candidates.title: Perspectives on traumatic brain injury screening among intersecting underserved populations: an exploratory study.
candidates.abstract: This study aimed to explore barriers and facilitators in traumatic brain injury (TBI) screening for underserved individuals and knowledge translation efforts to address challenges. Guided by qualitative description, we conducted four virtual focus groups: 10 people (7 female, 3 male) with lived experience of precarious housing, criminal legal involvement, and/or violence and 11 service providers (9 female, 2 male) supporting these populations with TBI. Data were analyzed using thematic analysis. Barriers to TBI screening included (1) inconsistent implementation and competing priorities within organizations; (2) stigmatization and systemic challenges in service provision; and (3) a lack of a universal screening system and follow-up pathways. While potential facilitators to screening involved language, knowledge and resources, as identified in the following themes: (1) language matters: shaping conversations in TBI screening; (2) screening for all: knowledge and access; and (3) easy and engaging tools for screening. Barriers to TBI screening persist. Systemic changes and targeted educational initiatives are needed to improve knowledge and awareness of TBI with sensitivity to potential circumstances of specific populations. Affirming conversational language in screening, along with providing tailored resources and access to follow-up support services that address social determinants of health, are essential.

candidates.title: Beyond Digoxin Toxicity: A Fatal Case of BRASH Syndrome Triggered by Community-Acquired Pneumonia.
candidates.abstract: Bradycardia, renal failure, atrioventricular (AV) nodal blockade, shock, and hyperkalemia (BRASH) syndrome is a rare, life-threatening clinical condition caused by the synergistic interaction between hyperkalemia, renal dysfunction, and AV nodal blocking agents, resulting in severe bradycardia and hemodynamic instability. Early recognition is often challenging due to its nonspecific presentation. We report the case of an 82-year-old man with atrial fibrillation, ischemic heart disease, congestive cardiac failure, chronic kidney disease, and chronic digoxin therapy who presented with abdominal pain, confusion, dizziness, hypotension, and profound bradycardia. Investigations demonstrated severe hyperkalemia, acute kidney injury on top of chronic kidney disease, hyponatremia, and electrocardiographic changes consistent with hyperkalemia. Initial differential diagnoses included mesenteric ischemia, adrenal insufficiency, and digoxin toxicity; however, imaging excluded bowel ischemia, cortisol levels were normal, and serum digoxin at the therapeutic level. Community-acquired pneumonia complicated by sepsis was identified as the precipitating trigger for BRASH syndrome. Despite intensive treatment, including hyperkalemia management, isoprenaline infusion, antibiotics, corticosteroids, and supportive care, the patient's condition progressively deteriorated, culminating in multiorgan failure and death shortly afterward. This case highlights the diagnostic complexity of BRASH syndrome and emphasizes the importance of early recognition and targeted management to interrupt the vicious cycle and improve clinical outcomes.

candidates.title: Late HIV Diagnosis and Delayed Antiretroviral Therapy Prescription in Routine Care Within a Mexican Social-Security Network.
candidates.abstract: BackgroundLate HIV diagnosis and delayed antiretroviral therapy (ART) prescription hinder care. We estimated frequencies and patient-level associations.MethodsWe retrospectively analyzed 137 records from a family-medicine source in southeastern Mexico (2021-2023). Outcomes were late diagnosis (CD4 <350 cells/µL or WHO/PAHO stage III-IV) and delayed first ART prescription (>30 days after confirmed diagnosis). Modified Poisson regression estimated adjusted prevalence ratios.ResultsLate diagnosis was classifiable in 129 records and present in 104 (80.6%; 95% CI, 73.0%-86.5%). Prescription timing was available in 120; 86 (71.7%; 95% CI, 63.0%-79.0%) exceeded 30 days. Medium and low education each had a 40% higher adjusted prevalence of late diagnosis than high education. No covariate was associated with delayed prescription.ConclusionsBoth outcomes were common. Education was associated with late diagnosis; no measured patient-level variable was independently associated with prescription delay. Care-process determinants require prospective measurement. Starting HIV treatment soon after diagnosis helps people stay healthy and reduces the chance of passing HIV to others. However, late diagnosis and delays in prescribing treatment can still occur in routine care. This study reviewed 137 medical records of adults with confirmed HIV infection from a social-security health-care network in southeastern Mexico between 2021 and 2023. We examined whether HIV was diagnosed after substantial effects on the immune system had already occurred and how much time passed between confirmed HIV diagnosis and the first treatment prescription recorded in the medical record. Among 129 records that could be classified, late HIV diagnosis was identified in 104 (80.6%). Among 120 records with both dates available, 71.7% had their first treatment prescription recorded more than 30 days after diagnosis. The median interval was 53.5 days. Educational level was associated with late diagnosis, but the patient information available in routine records did not clearly explain differences in prescription timing. The records did not consistently contain information about several parts of the care process that could contribute to delays, so the study cannot determine their causes. These findings describe this specific health-care population and should not be interpreted as estimates for all people living with HIV in Mexico. They also show how routine medical records can be used to monitor late diagnosis and prescription timing and to identify questions that require more detailed study.
candidates.journal: Journal of the International Association of Providers of AIDS Care

candidates.title: How to Practice Open Science: A Cookbook for Clinical Psychology and Psychotherapy Research.
candidates.abstract: Even though Open Science practices advance the credibility and accessibility of knowledge gained through research, they are not yet as common in clinical psychology as in other subfields of psychology. This paper presents an overview of how to implement Open Science practices in clinical psychology and psychotherapy research. We will address frequently encountered challenges and present different ways to deal with sensitive topics within the specific field. We explain Open Science practices while planning a study, during data collection and preparation of a publication, and for the publication of results. Finally, we will show options for how to structure a whole research group in support of Open Science practices. With different types of actions - of varying degrees of complexity and openness - we can continually and ethically move toward more Open Science, which will strengthen clinical research and is therefore essential for people with lived experiences of psychological symptoms, patients, psychotherapists, and for investments in psychological treatments.

candidates.title: CLDN18.2 ADCs "A Real Step Forward" for Stomach Cancer.
candidates.abstract: Results from two phase III trials, CLARITY-Gastric01 and G-HOPE-001, indicate that the investigational CLDN18.2-targeting antibody-drug conjugates sonesitatug vedotin and arcotatug tavatecan could be effective third- or later-line treatments for patients with CLDN18.2-positive gastric or gastroesophageal carcinomas. Both ADCs improved overall survival, which is welcome news for a population whose options are otherwise very limited.
